prompt_text: Who is the best dentist in Kansas City Missouri for a dental implant?
answer_verbatim:
I can’t single out one absolute “best” dentist for implants in Kansas City — the right provider depends on your exact needs (single tooth vs full-arch, bone grafting needs, sedation preference, budget and insurance). I can, however, help you find the best option for you and give guidance on how to choose.

Quick guidance
- Prefer a specialist for implants: oral & maxillofacial surgeons, periodontists, or prosthodontists typically have the most training for implants and complex cases. Some general dentists with advanced implant training also do excellent work.
- Look for board certification or fellowship and years of implant experience. Memberships in AAID, AAP, or American College of Prosthodontists and/or ABOI/ID certification are good signals.
- Make sure they use CBCT (3D) imaging and digital treatment planning; ask about the implant system/brand they use.
- Check patient before/after photos and independent reviews (Google, Healthgrades, Yelp).
- Ask about who performs each step (surgery vs crown) and whether they do full digital workflows if you want immediate or same-day teeth options.
- Ask about success rate, number of implants placed per year, complications policy, sedation options, and costs/financing.

Questions to ask a prospective implant provider
- How many implant surgeries do you perform per year?
- Are you a board-certified oral surgeon/periodontist/prosthodontist? If not, what implant training do you have?
- Do you use CBCT and digital surgical guides?
- What implant system/brand do you use and why?
- Who will make the final crown (in-house prosthodontist or a referring dentist)?
- What’s your success/complication rate and warranty for implant restorations?
- Estimated total cost for implant + abutment + crown and whether bone grafting/sinus lift is included.

Red flags
- Provider avoids discussing implant brand, imaging, or complication rates.
- No follow-up plan or not willing to coordinate with your restorative dentist.
- Extremely low fees with no explanation (may indicate lower-quality materials/technique).

How I can help right now
If you’d like, tell me:
- Your ZIP code or neighborhood in Kansas City
- Whether you have dental insurance and its name (or if you’re paying out of pocket)
- The type of implant you need (single tooth, multiple, full arch)

I’ll look up well-reviewed specialists near you (oral surgeons, periodontists, prosthodontists), show their credentials and patient ratings, and give a short comparison. Which ZIP or neighborhood should I search?
